Sulfites are compounds containing the sulfite ion (SO3²⁻). They are commonly used as preservatives in food and beverages.

From a chemical reactivity perspective, sulfites are known for their ability to donate electrons in chemical reactions, making them reducing agents. They can be oxidized to sulfates (SO4²⁻). This reducing property is why sulfites are used as preservatives - they can prevent oxidation reactions in foods.

Sulfites readily react with oxygen, hydrogen peroxide, and other oxidizing agents. They can reduce many compounds and are themselves oxidized in the process. This is a characteristic property of reducing agents.

Therefore, sulfites belong to the reactivity group of reducing agents.
